validity.recommendation: Treat P6964 as unconfirmed pending further sourcing; investigate whether it is a phantom/duplicate artifact of P6963 (the same PipelineName/endpoints, one row per status) rather than a distinct, pre-existing physical pipeline.
validity.researcher_notes: GEM records P6964 as 'Segment I, operating' of the Yangiyer-Ahangaran Gas Pipeline, paired with P6963 'Segment II, construction' (95 km, dia 1220mm, ConstructionYear=2022). P6964 itself carries NO other data on the sheet -- no length, diameter, capacity, StartYear1, or Owner -- only Status=operating and the shared start/end locations. All four of the wiki-harvested current refs on this row were checked directly and every one describes the NEW 95 km line, not a pre-existing segment: gazeta.uz 2022-12-30 ('Uztransgaz launched construction of a trunk gas pipeline... Yangiyer-Ahangaran, 95 km, dia 1220mm, >47 km of pipe delivered, 6 km installed, commissioning planned Q3 2023') and gazeta.uz 2023-09-30 ('construction continues on another project -- a NEW line [novoi nitki] 95 km long in the Yangiyer-Ahangaran direction') are both explicitly about the new construction project (P6963's story), not confirmation that an older 'Segment I' already operates. The minenergy.uz/1629 press-tour piece cited as the second Status ref is now a soft-404 (HTTP 200 but a client-rendered Next.js 'not found' page, confirmed by direct fetch) -- inaccessible, not a confirmed 404/410, so I am not treating it as deleted, but it currently supports nothing. gem.wiki's own page (read for leads only, never cited) frames Segment I as 'the existing pipeline' but admits 'capacity, length, diameter, and start year are not specified in available documentation' -- i.e. GEM staff never actually sourced a distinct pre-2022 entity, they appear to have inferred one from the framing of the 2022 construction announcements as an 'improvement' project. I searched extensively in Russian for an older/original Yangiyer-Ahangaran line predating the 2022 project (utg.uz history and press pages -- utg.uz/ru/about/history/ 404s; liting.uz / O'ZLITINEFTGAZ institute project lists -- garbled/unreliable OCR text, discounted as a source; ru.wikipedia.org Uztransgaz article -- names only the Ahangaran-Pungan line, 2007-2010, 165 km, through Kamchik pass, with the same Ahangaran compressor station; regnum.ru -- blocked 403) and found nothing that independently names a physically distinct, already-operating 'Yangiyer-Ahangaran' pipeline before the 2022 project. The most economical reading of the evidence is that the Dec-2022 project is the FIRST direct Yangiyer-Ahangaran line, and gas previously reached the Ahangaran hub by other routes (e.g. via the broader trunk network feeding into Ahangaran, from which Ahangaran-Pungan continues into the Fergana valley proper) that were never named 'Yangiyer-Ahangaran'. I could not confirm this either way with a source explicitly stating one-pipeline-not-two, so I am not asserting P6964 = P6963 as a firm duplicate (no source affirmatively describes them as one pipe, which the standing rule requires before flagging duplicate) -- but the existence of a distinct, already-operating Segment I is unconfirmed and should not be presented as sourced fact. No fills are staged for P6964's blank spec fields given this open existence question.

validity.recommendation: Correct StartState/Province from 'Fergana' to 'Sirdaryo' (Sirdaryo Region) -- Yangiyer is not in Fergana. This affects P6964 and, on the same evidence, its sibling row P6963 (out of this batch's scope but sharing the same StartLocation/StartState fields).
validity.researcher_notes: GEM lists StartLocation=Yangiyer, StartState/Province=Fergana for both P6963 and P6964. Yangiyer is a city in Sirdaryo (Syrdarya) Region, Uzbekistan (est. 1957 in the Hungry Steppe/Mirzachoʻl reclamation project, at approx. 40.27N 68.82E), NOT in Fergana Region -- confirmed independently by English Wikipedia, Russian Wikipedia, and Wikidata, corroborated further by multiple independent Uzbek gazetteer sites (tochka-na-karte.ru, geo.koltyrin.ru, geogoroda.ru) that all place it in Syrdarya oblast. This is consistent with the pipeline's actual function: it is a feeder INTO the Ahangaran hub (Tashkent region) from the trunk-system side near Sirdaryo/Tashkent, not a line running within the Fergana valley itself -- the Fergana-valley gas supply is the downstream beneficiary via the separate Ahangaran-Pungan line through the Kamchik pass, which is what the press coverage's 'improves gas supply to Fergana/Namangan/Andijan' language actually refers to. EndLocation=Ahangaran / EndState/Province=Tashkent is correct and not in question. | POLICY (source_roster.md: Wikipedia is never cited directly; studfile.net is a tertiary re-upload host, same class as the blocklisted wikidot). The Yangiyer pages cited here are EVIDENCE for this concern, not a proposed [ref] cell, and the concern stands on its merits. But before the correction is applied to the sheet the geographic fact needs a citable source (GeoNames or the Uzbek statistics committee) — do not paste a Wikipedia URL into a [ref] cell.

status_reviews.researcher_notes: Cannot confirm the recorded 'operating' status because I cannot confirm the underlying entity -- see the existence concern in validity[]. All dated, independent evidence found for anything called 'Yangiyer-Ahangaran' (gazeta.uz 2022-12-30, gazeta.uz 2023-09-30) concerns the NEW 95 km line (P6963, status=construction, most recently reported still in progress August 2025 per gem.wiki), not a separate already-operating Segment I. No independent source of any date confirms a distinct pre-2022 Yangiyer-Ahangaran pipeline was ever built or is currently operating, so there is no dated evidence to apply the confirm/change/stale framework to. This is not a dormancy case (the row is 'operating', not proposed/shelved) so the staleness rules do not apply either. Recommend Update treat this as an existence question first, not a routine status re-verification.

summary: P6964 (Yangiyer-Ahangaran Segment I, operating) is an existence concern: every discoverable source describing 'Yangiyer-Ahangaran' -- including the sheet's own cited refs -- is actually about the NEW 95 km line under construction since Dec 2022 (P6963), and no independent source confirms a distinct, already-operating predecessor line; GEM's own wiki page admits length/diameter/capacity/start year are unsourced for Segment I. Also flagged: StartState/Province='Fergana' is wrong for both P6963 and P6964 -- Yangiyer is in Sirdaryo Region (2 independent geographic sources). No fills staged pending the existence question; status review verdict is unclear for the same reason.
